clue.text: Spooner's happy smiling at wedding, maybe

definitions.note: a wedding is one example of a formal rite, hence 'maybe'

indicators.note: the possessive of Spooner says the opening sounds of the next two words are to be swapped

parts.note: happy means merry
a smiling face is a sunny one

explanation.surface: A Spooner remark about looking cheerful and beaming at a marriage.
explanation.walkthrough: Swap the first sounds of MERRY and SUNNY to hear SERRY MUNNY, which is spelt as the answer; the second half only approximates the sound.
explanation.definitionFit: A wedding is an example of a formal rite performed with set ritual.

clue.text: Chancellor follows report of borrowing total; his sort have been E for a year and a day

clue.text: E bird — Grand Peregrine not right — disoriented in relay
